messages:
Riley T.: Hey folks — due date 7/2, planning to start parental leave 6/20 for 10 weeks. Quick Qs: paperwork deadlines, whether I should open a backfill req now, and how this affects my end-of-quarter performance ratings.
Priya (People Ops): Congrats Riley! :tada: Paperwork: file LOA in Workday at least 2 pay periods before 6/20 (so aim for 6/6). Attach medical cert if FMLA applies. For performance: being on approved leave does not automatically block ratings or promo. Managers should include your contribution window in the calibration notes.
Riley T.: If I do a partial return (60% first month) do I need to indicate that now?
Priya (People Ops): You can note intent in the LOA but final phased-return schedules are approved later. Put the preference in the comments and well follow up.
Omar (Payroll): Important: for bonus proration we consider paid payroll months. If you select company_topup we count those weeks as paid for proration. LOA must be coded correctly before payroll cutoff (5/30) to avoid manual fixes.
Sasha (Hiring Ops): Backfill: if you want a contractor overlap, start the req now. For a 10-week leave we usually recommend a 2-week overlap for handoff. If Riley wants Hiring Ops to draft the contractor brief, say so and well pull recruiters.
Riley T.: Yes please draft a contractor brief — will list priority tasks. Also, who handles recurring calendar invites while Im out?
Priya (People Ops): Manager should reassign recurring meetings; please create a handoff doc listing owners for oncall, weekly syncs, and key deliverables. Attach it to the LOA request in Workday.
hr-bot: Reminder: Workday LOA deadline 2025-06-06 (automated).
Riley T.: Thanks everyone — Ill submit LOA today and put the handoff doc in the LOA comments.
